_why: Two guards, and they are load-bearing for each other: a marker-less poll is only safe because --out is written atomically, and an atomic write only matters because something polls for the file. Mutating either alone must fail, which is what pins the pair.

mutations.name: marker-less-becomes-the-default
mutations._mechanism: Flip the opt-in and every existing report-wait caller silently loses the .done contract -- the one thing keeping a half-written report unreadable. Nobody asked for that, and nothing in their invocation would show it changed.

mutations.name: an-empty-file-counts-as-complete
mutations._mechanism: With the marker gone, non-emptiness is the ONLY integrity check left. Drop it and a freshly-created zero-byte file reads as a finished report -- exactly what a `>` redirect produces at the instant it truncates.
mutations.find: if marker_ok and os.path.isfile(path) and os.path.getsize(path) > 0:

mutations.name: out-is-written-non-atomically-again
mutations._mechanism: The half the poller's correctness rests on. A plain cp can be observed mid-copy, so the marker-less poll -- which trusts the file's appearance -- reads a truncated verdict as a real one. Restores the race the .done marker was invented to prevent, by another door. Pinned by a STRUCTURAL assertion because atomicity has no externally observable trace that cp+rm does not also produce -- this mutation is what proved the behavioural tests could not see it.

mutations.name: the-temp-crosses-a-filesystem
mutations._mechanism: Same-directory is what makes the rename atomic. Put the temp in /tmp and `mv` silently degrades to copy-then-unlink across a filesystem boundary -- the race returns while the code still reads as atomic. Re-anchored when the $$ temp was replaced by mktemp to fix a collision the full suite caught; --check-anchors refused rather than measuring nothing.

mutations.name: one-temp-path-for-every-write
mutations._mechanism: The bug this helper shipped with for one suite run. `$$` is constant across every --out a single wrapper invocation writes, and audit-cycle writes one per pass -- so two writes share a temp and one clobbers the other. audit-cycle silently lost its p1 report. Fixing a race by adding a race.
